'''Emilija Mlakar Branc''' (10 November 1901 – 25 June 1989) was a [[Slovenes|Slovenian]] [[mathematician]], [[Professor|mathematics professor]], and [[Mathematics education|author of mathematics textbooks]]. In 1928, she became the first woman to graduate in mathematics from the [[University of Ljubljana]].<ref name=":11">{{Cite web|title=Okrogla miza ob Dnevu žensk v matematiki v sredo, 15. maja|url=https://www.dmfa.si/odrustvu/NovicaPrikaz.aspx?itemid=793|website=www.dmfa.si|accessdate=2026-02-26|date=2024|publisher=DMFA Slovenije|language=sl|trans-title=Round table on Women in Mathematics Day on Wednesday, 15 May}}</ref> She was the author and co-author of several textbooks on [[geometry]] and [[solid geometry]], which were popular and reprinted several times.<ref name=":12">{{Cite web|title=Emilija Branc|url=https://bib.cobiss.net/bibliographies/si/webBiblio/bib201_20260225_175740_a44338275.html|website=bib.cobiss.net|accessdate=2026-02-26|language=sl|trans-title=Emilija Branc}}</ref>

== Childhood ==
She was born on 10 November 1901 in [[Ptuj]], where her family had moved in 1899 from [[Moškanjci]].<ref name=":8" /><ref name=":9" /> There, her mother Marjeta Beg had worked in an inn, while her father Štefan Mlakar worked as a stationmaster.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web|title=Krstna knjiga / Taufbuch - 02146 {{!}} 147 Ptuj - Sv. Peter in Pavel {{!}} Nadškofija Maribor {{!}} Slovenia {{!}} Matricula Online|url=https://data.matricula-online.eu/sl/slovenia/maribor/ptuj-sv-peter-in-pavel/02146/?pg=87|website=data.matricula-online.eu|accessdate=2026-02-27|date=1900–1903|publisher=Archdiocesan Archives Maribor|language=sl|trans-title=Baptismal Register / Taufbuch – 02146 {{!}} 147 Ptuj - Sv. Peter in Pavel {{!}} Nadškofija Maribor {{!}} Slovenia {{!}} Matricula Online}}</ref><ref name=":9">{{Cite journal|last=Švajncer|first=Janez J.|date=1990|title=Albin Mlakar – pozabljeni vojak|url=https://dlib.si/details/URN:NBN:SI:DOC-455UDDYN|journal=Kronika|language=sl|volume=1/2|pages=50–55|trans-title=Albin Mlakar – the forgotten soldier}}</ref> She had twelve brothers and sisters, eight of whom reached adulthood. Among them was the later Austro-Hungarian army officer {{ill|Albin Mlakar|sl}} (1890–1946).<ref name=":9" /> Her parents sent all their surviving children to school, including Emilija, who graduated high school in 1924.<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":13">{{Cite book|title=Stalež šolstva in učiteljstva ter prosvetnih in kulturnih ustanov v Dravski banovini|publisher=Banovinska zaloga šolskih knjig in učil, Ljubljana|year=1934|url=https://www.sistory.si/publication/1148|pages=20–21|chapter=3. State Real Gymnasium in Kranj|language=sl|trans-title=State of education, teachers, and educational and cultural institutions in the Drava Banovina}}</ref>

== Education ==
After completing primary and secondary education, she enrolled in the study of mathematics, pedagogical track, at the {{ill|Faculty of Arts in Ljubljana|lt=Faculty of Arts|sl|Filozofska fakulteta v Ljubljani}} at [[University of Ljubljana]]; at that time, the faculty offered no other mathematics programme.<ref name=":14">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sistory.si/popis/97f2fa0b-bdbf-4ec2-90c3-483fee1c5993/enota/2/1a9675a5-e8aa-4f5e-994f-cc41333eab19?p=9|website=www.sistory.si|accessdate=2026-02-26|title=Popis prebivalstva Ljubljane|date=1928|publisher=City of Ljubljana|language=sl|trans-title=Census of the population of Ljubljana}}</ref><ref name=":11" /><ref name=":17">{{Cite journal|date=December 1967|title=Diplome iz matematike in astronomije na univerzi v Ljubljani|url=http://lkrv.fri.uni-lj.si/~ajurisic/omf_1-54/ocr/omf14_2ocr.pdf|journal=Obzornik za matematiko in fiziko|language=sl|location=Ljubljana|volume=2|pages=85–88|trans-title=Degrees in mathematics and astronomy at the University of Ljubljana}}</ref> During her studies, she lived as a lodger in an apartment in Ljubljana together with her younger brother, who was then a secondary-school student.<ref name=":14" /> At the faculty, one of her classmates was Janko Branc (1902–1963) from [[Kranjska Gora]], later a lecturer in mathematics at the Faculty of Natural Sciences and Technology, whom she married on 14 July 1928.<ref name=":8" /><ref name=":10">{{Cite journal|last=Vidav|first=Ivan|author-link=Ivan Vidav|date=November 1963|title=Višji predavatelj Janko Branc|url=http://www.obzornik.si/omf_1-54/ocr/omf10_3ocr.pdf|journal=Obzornik za matematiko in fiziko|language=sl|volume=3|page=136|trans-title=Senior lecturer Janko Branc}}</ref> They had no children (at least none who survived to adulthood).<ref name=":7">{{Cite news|title=Emilija Branc – Osmrtnica|date=27 June 1989|url=https://www.dlib.si/details/URN:NBN:SI:DOC-0E4UX47T|newspaper=Delo|volume=147|page=15|language=sl|trans-title=Emilija Branc – obituary}}</ref> In 1928 she became the first woman, and the thirteenth person overall, to graduate in mathematics from the University of Ljubljana.<ref name=":11" /><ref>{{Cite news|title=Izvestje državne klasične gimnazije v Ljubljani za šolsko leto 1937/38|date=1938|pages=4–5|publisher=State Classical Gymnasium, Ljubljana|location=Ljubljana|url=https://www.sistory.si/publication/41317|newspaper=Izvestje državne klasične gimnazije v Ljubljani|language=sl|trans-title=Report of the State Classical Gymnasium in Ljubljana for the school year 1937/38}}</ref><ref name=":15">{{Cite news|title=Izvestje državne klasične gimnazije v Ljubljani za šolsko leto 1933/34|date=1934|pages=3–7|publisher=State Classical Gymnasium, Ljubljana|location=Ljubljana|url=https://www.dlib.si/details/URN:NBN:SI:DOC-RU8GXLCL/|newspaper=Izvestje državne klasične gimnazije v Ljubljani|language=sl|trans-title=Report of the State Classical Gymnasium in Ljubljana for the school year 1933/34}}</ref><ref name=":16">{{Cite news|title=Učiteljski zbor|date=1940|publisher=State Women’s Real Gymnasium in Ljubljana|language=sl|url=https://www.dlib.si/details/URN:NBN:SI:DOC-67POT4IV|pages=3–9|newspaper=Izvestje državne ženske realne gimnazije|trans-title=Teaching staff}}</ref><ref name=":17" />

== Career ==
After graduating university, she was employed in 1929 as a teacher at the State Real Gymnasium of Crown Prince Andrew in Ptuj (now [[Gimnazija Ptuj]]).<ref>{{Cite news|title=Klasifikacija|date=1930|page=21–26|url=https://www.dlib.si/details/URN:NBN:SI:DOC-3EWN7GAK|publisher=State Real Gymnasium of Crown Prince Andrew in Ptuj|newspaper=Izvestje Državne realne gimnazije kraljeviča Andreja|language=sl|trans-title=Classification}}</ref> In 1930 she became an assistant in physics at the {{ill|Technical Faculty in Ljubljana|lt=Technical Faculty|sl|Tehniška fakulteta v Ljubljani}} in Ljubljana,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sistory.si/popis/48099995-4c4a-46b8-bfa2-834c8176cd82/enota/2/8bf9db4b-8406-4ce2-8b88-758bbf9f620b?p=1|website=www.sistory.si|accessdate=2026-02-26|title=Popis prebivalstva Ljubljane|date=1931|publisher=City of Ljubljana|language=sl|trans-title=Census of the population of Ljubljana}}</ref>{{Efn|From 1919 to 1925, enrolment in the study of mathematics and physics was combined. Anyone who successfully completed it with a diploma examination, in which both subjects were equal main subjects, became both a mathematician and a physicist and had the right to teach both subjects in all classes of a gymnasium.}} where she worked until 1933.<ref name=":13" /> In 1932, she passed the professorial examination at the University of Ljubljana and earned the title of professor.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Osebne vesti|date=3 July 1932|newspaper=Slovenec|language=sl|page=5|publisher=Ljudska tiskarna|volume=149|url=https://www.dlib.si/details/URN:NBN:SI:DOC-7TEQ61F0|trans-title=Personal news}}</ref>

In 1933, she was employed as a teacher of mathematics and physics at the State Real Gymnasium in Kranj (now the {{ill|Gimnazija Kranj|lt=Gimnazija Kranj|sl|Gimnazija Kranj}}), where she remained for one year.<ref name=":13" /> In 1934, she was transferred to the {{ill|State Classical Gymnasium in Ljubljana|lt=State Classical Gymnasium|sl|Klasična gimnazija v Ljubljani}} in Ljubljana, where she worked as a teacher of mathematics and physics until 1937, when she was transferred to the State Women’s Real Gymnasium (now [[Gimnazija Poljane]]).<ref name=":13" /><ref name=":15" /><ref name=":16" /> There, in addition to teaching mathematics and physics, she also served as business manager and custodian of the physics collection, the teachers' library, and the library of the support society.<ref name=":16" />

Between 1952 and 1955, as a member of the [[Society of Mathematicians, Physicists and Astronomers of Slovenia|DMFA]] (Society of Mathematicians, Physicists and Astronomers of Slovenia), she also taught mathematics, alongside her full-time job, in a general educational course in mathematics and physics under the auspices of the People’s University.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Jubilejni zbornik ob 60-letnici DMFA Slovenije, Bled, 6.–7. 11. 2009|publisher=DMFA|year=2009|pages=5–52|language=sl|url=https://www.dmfa.si/ODrustvu/Dokumenti/OZ2009-Bilten.pdf|chapter=Overview of the activities of DMFA Slovenia|issn=1318-8429|trans-title=Jubilee proceedings on the 60th anniversary of DMFA Slovenia, Bled, 6–7 November 2009}}</ref> Among her students there was the later chemist [[Aleksandra Kornhauser Frazer]], who later said that Emilija Mlakar Branc had "initiated her into logical thinking for life".<ref>{{Cite web|title=V spomin legendarni AKF|url=https://blog.cobiss.si/2020/10/26/v-spomin-legendarni-akf/|website=Blog COBISS|accessdate=2026-02-27|language=sl|first=Franci|last=Pivec|date=26 October 2020|trans-title=In memory of the legendary AKF}}</ref>

Between 1937 and 1952, Branc wrote, alone and with co-authors, four textbooks on [[geometry]] and two collections of exercises in [[solid geometry]], which were popular in Slovenian lands and reprinted several times.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=Geometrija za tretji in četrti razred srednjih šol|last=Ziegler|first=Milan|publisher=Jugoslovanska knjigarna|year=1937|location=Ljubljana|last2=Žabkar|first2=Albin|last3=Mlakar Branc|first3=Emilija|language=sl|author-link3=Emilija Mlakar Branc|trans-title=Geometry for the Third and Fourth Grades of Secondary Schools}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite book|title=Geometrija za nižje razrede srednjih šol. Del 1.|last=Mlakar Branc|first=Emilija|publisher=Državna založba Slovenije|year=1947|location=Ljubljana|last2=Jelenc|first2=Slavica|last3=Ziegler|first3=Milan|last4=Žabkar|first4=Albin|language=sl|author-link=Emilija Mlakar Branc|trans-title=Geometry for the Lower Grades of Secondary Schools, Part 1}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite book|title=Geometrija za nižje razrede srednjih šol. Del 2.|last=Mlakar Branc|first=Emilija|publisher=Državna založba Slovenije|year=1947|location=Ljubljana|last2=Jelenc|first2=Slavica|last3=Ziegler|first3=Milan|last4=Žabkar|first4=Albin|language=sl|author-link=Emilija Mlakar Branc|trans-title=Geometry for the Lower Grades of Secondary Schools, Part 2}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite book|title=Geometrija za nižje razrede srednjih šol. Del 3.|last=Mlakar Branc|first=Emilija|publisher=Državna založba Slovenije|year=1947|location=Ljubljana|last2=Jelenc|first2=Slavica|last3=Ziegler|first3=Milan|last4=Žabkar|first4=Albin|language=sl|author-link=Emilija Mlakar Branc|trans-title=Geometry for the Lower Grades of Secondary Schools, Part 3}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite book|title=Geometrija za nižje razrede srednjih šol: IV. del|last=Mlakar Branc|first=Emilija|publisher=Državna založba Slovenije|year=1952|location=Ljubljana|last2=Jelenc|first2=Slavica|last3=Ziegler|first3=Milan|last4=Žabkar|first4=Albin|language=sl|author-link=Emilija Mlakar Branc|trans-title=Geometry for the Lower Grades of Secondary Schools, Part IV}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite book|title=Zbirka nalog iz planimetrije in stereometrije: I. in II. del|last=Mlakar Branc|first=Emilija|publisher=Državna založba Slovenije|year=1947|location=Ljubljana|last2=Čemažar|first2=Franc|author-link=Emilija Mlakar Branc|language=Sl|trans-title=Collection of Exercises in Plane Geometry and Solid Geometry: Parts I and II}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite book|title=Vaje iz stereometrije|last=Mlakar Branc|first=Emilija|publisher=Državna založba Slovenije|year=1952|location=Ljubljana|language=sl|author-link=Emilija Mlakar Branc|trans-title=Exercises in Solid Geometry}}</ref><ref name=":12" />

== Later life and death ==
In 1963, her husband died after a long illness.<ref name=":10" /> After retirement, she moved to live with relatives in Ptuj. She died on 25 June 1989 in Ptuj.<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":8" /> She was buried at Rogoznica Cemetery in Ptuj.<ref name=":7" />
